# Secrets Bridge

> Secrets Bridge adds access requests, approvals and audit to the secrets you keep in AWS Secrets Manager and HashiCorp Vault. Values stay in your provider.

Secrets Bridge is a secrets control plane. It adds access requests, approvals, RBAC, policy, audit and agent execution around the secrets a team already keeps in AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault. It keeps requests, approvals and audit metadata; secret values stay in the provider, and the agent runs inside the team's infrastructure and only connects out. Azure Key Vault and GCP Secret Manager are on the roadmap. It is open source and pre-1.0: see Product status for what works today.

Every page below is also available as Markdown at the linked URL, and https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/llms-full.txt has all of them in one file.

---

Source: https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/

# Govern who uses your secrets.

Secrets Bridge adds access requests, approvals, audit and agent execution
around the secrets you already keep in AWS Secrets Manager and HashiCorp
Vault. We keep requests, approvals and audit metadata. Your secret values
stay in your provider.

[Run it locally](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/docker-compose/)
[Read the architecture](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/architecture/)
Source on GitHub

Open source and pre-1.0. See what is live today and what is still on the roadmap.

## We keep

- Requests, and who approved them
- The audit trail: who, what, when and why
- Which secret paths and key names a project may use

## We never keep

- Secret values in plain text. In transit a value exists only as an encrypted, single-use wrap with a short lifetime.
- Provider credentials. The agent uses its own, inside your infrastructure.

The agent runs inside your infrastructure and only calls out, so you open no inbound port.

## Where your secrets go, and where they don't

Values stay in your provider until an approved request needs them. Then they travel once, sealed, and only to the person who asked. Pick a step to follow it.

## What it holds to
These are enforced in code, not left to policy. The threat model shows how each boundary is kept.

- No plaintext values in the control plane. Not in Postgres, Redis, logs, audit events or the browser. In transit, values are KMS-wrapped.
- The agent only calls out. No inbound port, no database, no Kubernetes API access to Secrets.
- Production never allows direct reveal. The refusal is enforced in code and audited.
- Values move once. KMS-wrapped, single-use, short-lived, and opened only by the right person.
- Audit is append-only and metadata-only. Who, what, when and why, never the value.
- Agents are bound and revocable. One-time enrollment tokens, one provider connection per agent, revoked at once.

## What works today

### Implemented

- AWS Secrets Manager and HashiCorp Vault through the agent
- Read requests with policy-driven approval
- Direct reveal in non-production, behind a second factor
- Cross-team requests: another team supplies the values
- Agent enrollment, status and revoke
- Append-only audit trail

### Roadmap

- Azure Key Vault and GCP Secret Manager providers
- Deeper Kubernetes External Secrets integration
- Flux integration
- Agents that claim only their own connection's jobs

Not shipped. Don't plan around these yet.

Full product status, with what is QA-certified and what is in progress.

## Start on your laptop

The api repo's compose file starts Postgres, Redis and the control plane; the console and the agent run from their own repos. The local guide walks through the whole flow against a dev Vault.

[Run it locally](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/docker-compose/)
[Operations guide](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/)

Source: https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/

# Overview

Secrets Bridge is a **secrets control plane**: the layer that sits
between developers / operators and the actual secret stores. The
mental model the project never violates:

```
Control Plane = decisions, workflow, metadata, audit, RBAC, jobs, status
Agent         = execution inside the target account/cluster, least privilege
Providers     = the actual secret values (source of truth)
```

The Control Plane never holds raw secret values. The Agent holds
them for the duration of one request and then drops them. The
Providers are unchanged. Secrets Bridge augments them, it doesn't
replace them.

## The flows the platform supports today

| Flow | Direction | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Read** | provider → user | Developer requests a value; workflow approves; agent fetches; CP stores a single-use KMS-wrapped envelope; UI reveals it once. |
| **Patch** | user → provider | Developer submits a new value through the form; workflow approves; agent GET-merge-PUTs to the provider so untouched keys survive. |
| **Discovery** | provider → CP catalog | Admin enqueues a discover job; agent calls `ListMetadata`; CP upserts to the `secrets` table with native provider labels preserved verbatim (Vault `custom_metadata`, AWS Tags, GCP labels, Azure tags). |
| **Gateway observation** | Argo CD → Gateway → CP | After an approved change reaches the provider, an optional [Gateway](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/gateway/) inside your boundary reads Argo CD rollout state and reports it as metadata. Strictly read-only, off unless an environment's observation source is `gateway`. The CP itself never talks to Argo CD. Argo CD health is context, not proof the workload picked up the new value. |

## What ships today

| Repo | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [`core`](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/core/) | Shipped | Provider interface, Vault + AWS SM connectors, type-safe value redaction |
| [`api`](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/api/) | Shipped | Fiber v3 Control Plane API, Postgres + Redis, RBAC catalog, session-cookie login |
| [`agent`](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/agent/) | Shipped | Outbound-only, claim → wrap → execute → complete loop, X25519 wire envelope |
| [`worker`](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/worker/) | Shipped | Sweepers, scheduler, notifications, Gateway observation sweepers |
| [`controller`](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/controller/) | Shipped | Kubernetes CRD reconciler ported from v0.1.0 |
| [`ui`](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/ui/) | Shipped | React SPA: dashboard, requests, agents, admin, audit, secrets |
| [`gateway`](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/components/gateway/) | In progress | Release 1: read-only Argo CD observation. Binary, chart, registry, observation tasks, console and the cutover from the control-plane poller merged; not yet through QA |
| [`charts`](https://github.com/secrets-bridge/charts) | Shipped | Hardened Helm charts for the control plane and the agent, published to GHCR. The Gateway chart is part of Gateway Release 1 |
| [`docs`](https://github.com/secrets-bridge/docs) | You're reading it | mkdocs-material |

## What's intentionally out of scope

- **Replacing your secrets provider.** Vault, AWS SM, etc. stay
  authoritative. Secrets Bridge is a governance + access plane, not
  a value store.
- **Storing secret values.** The `secret_wraps` table holds
  KMS-encrypted envelopes for the duration of one request only
  (TTL in minutes/hours, single-shot consumption).
- **Writing K8s secrets from the CP.** The `controller` does
  GitOps-style sync; the CP itself never reaches into a cluster.
- **Providing a "central admin password" for every provider.** The
  agent uses **only** the credentials configured inside its own
  network boundary. The CP never holds provider master credentials.

## Next steps

- [The architecture in detail](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/architecture/)
- [Threat model and the hard rules we never break](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/overview/threat-model/)
- [Try the local docker-compose stack](https://secrets-bridge.io/latest/operations/docker-compose/)
